results.content:
At the heart of all LLMs is the transformer architecture, introduced in the “Attention Is All You Need” paper. Despite many variations and improvements since, it remains the foundation of state-of-the-art models. On the left below is the original decoder-only transformer, and on the right is the Llama-2 70B architecture, which illustrates some of these later refinements:

Transformers [...] There are some architectural differences to note. For example, LLaMA-2 70B uses Grouped Query Attention (GQA), a variant of attention that reduces memory demands. Most modern LLMs also place the normalisation layer before each block rather than after, which is different from the original Transformer. Still, the high-level flow remains the same: tokenised input goes in, contextualised embeddings come out. [...] For more details and examples, Google Research also put out this blog post to explain the concept in more detail.

In the original paper, speculative decoding demonstrated a 2×–3× wall-time speedup on models like T5-XXL, while maintaining identical output distributions.

### Description

Posted: 14 Dec 2025
PagedAttention is the “virtual memory” idea applied to LLM inference: instead of storing each request’s KV cache in one big contiguous chunk, vLLM breaks it into fixed-size blocks and maps logical tokens to physical GPU memory with a block table. The result is far less fragmentation, smarter reuse, and higher throughput under real, mixed-length traffic. [...] memory blocks as requests evolve. A scheduler implements continuous batching to keep the GPU busy. A KV cache manager tracks ownership and sharing, and it integrates cleanly with your stack. Subscribe for more LLM breakdowns. ### How do I choose between open-source and commercial embedding models for my RAG pipeline?

Start with deployment constraints and budget. Commercial APIs like OpenAI's text-embedding-3 scale automatically with zero infrastructure overhead but incur usage fees that grow with traffic.

# MMLU-Pro benchmark leaderboard: best LLM for general knowledge in 2026

 Jan 28, 2024
 2 min read

Updated: Feb 17

Ever wondered which AI model is best at general knowledge?

The main benchmark for this is MMLU-Pro.

It tests how well AI models handle questions across many academic and professional fields.

Not just math or science, but everything...

Law. Medicine. History. Business. Engineering.

This is one of the strongest benchmarks we have for broad reasoning. [...] MMLU-Pro is the upgraded version of MMLU.

It was introduced because models started saturating the original test.

The new benchmark raises the difficulty in three ways:

 12,000 graduate-level questions
 14 broad academic domains
 10 answer options per question instead of 4

MMLU-Pro focuses more on reasoning, not memorization.

It also reduces prompt sensitivity, meaning models cannot “game” the test as easily.
